title: Association of IL-6 (-174 C/G), TNF-α (-308 G/A), and IL-10 (-1082 G/A) Promoter Polymorphisms with Serum Cytokine Dynamics and Clinical Outcomes in Early-Onset Neonatal Sepsis: A Gestational Age-Stratified Study
content: Background/Objectives: Early-onset neonatal sepsis (EOS) remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality, particularly among preterm infants. This study aimed to evaluate perinatal risk factors, pre- and post-treatment serum cytokine kinetics (IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10), and promoter polymorphisms (IL-6 -174 C/G [rs1800795], TNF-α -308 G/A [rs1800629], and IL-10 -1082 G/A [rs1800896]) in term and preterm neonates with EOS from Uzbekistan. Methods: A case-control study was conducted involving 129 neonates with EOS (82 preterm, 47 term) and 66 healthy term controls. Serum IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10 concentrations were measured via ELISA before and after empirical antimicrobial therapy (n=82), and genotyping was performed using allele-specific PCR (n=140). Results: Preterm EOS infants showed higher rates of maternal urogenital infections (70.1%), intrapartum fever (86.5%), multiorgan complications, and mortality (28.0%), with third-trimester maternal COVID-19 strongly linked to fatal outcomes. Baseline IL-6 and TNF-α increased 3.7- and 3.2-fold in term EOS (p<0.001) and 3.2- and 2.7-fold in preterm EOS (p<0.001), whereas IL-10 peaked in preterm infants (2.1-fold; p<0.001). Post-treatment declines in IL-6 and TNF-α were blunted in preterm neonates (-14.2% and -12.0%) and Gram-negative sepsis. The IL-6 rs1800795 GG genotype increased EOS risk overall (OR=3.25, p=0.0007) and across term (OR = 2.86) and preterm (OR=3.93) strata, whereas CG was protective (OR=0.39). TNF-α rs1800629 GA increased EOS odds (OR=2.53, p=0.0266), while IL-10 rs1800896 showed no association. The (TNF-α + IL-6)/IL-10 index effectively stratified severity (3.5 in controls vs. 4.8 in preterm and ≥6.4 in term EOS). Conclusions: Integrating IL-6 and TNF-α genotyping with serial (TNF-α + IL-6)/IL-10 index monitoring enhances early risk stratification and severity prediction in neonatal sepsis.
